name: SSHole
tile_line: Exploited, in CISA KEV. Alpine-style sshd only.
tldr: A very long password logs in to key-only SSH accounts. Exploited within hours, on CISA's exploited list. Only on musl systems running sshd without PAM, mainly Alpine, if any account has a real password: upgrade openssh (Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora are safe).
summary: Password lengths that work differ by source: Alpine says 257 to 1024 bytes, the CVE record 256 to 1024 characters. It was disclosed on 5 Nov 2026, when OpenSSH 10.6p2 shipped a workaround; Alpine's cloud `alpine` user is one of the key-only accounts at risk.

affected.label: sshd uses musl libc
affected.text: Alpine and other musl-based systems, including Alpine containers that run sshd. glibc systems (Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, RHEL) and Dropbear are not affected. A line with `ld-musl` means musl.

affected.label: PAM off, password login on
affected.text: Alpine's `openssh-server` is built without PAM, so `sshd -T` prints no `usepam` line. `openssh-server-pam` with `UsePAM yes` is safe. `passwordauthentication yes` is the default. Run as root.

affected.label: A `*` account plus a real hash
affected.text: Some account has `*` as its password (key-only users, `root` since about Alpine 3.16 if `PermitRootLogin yes`, the `alpine` user in cloud images 3.18.11–3.24.3) and at least one account has a `$5$` or `$6$` hash. Directory-service users (nslcd, winbind, sssd) with no shadow entry also count, and the commands below miss them. Locked `!` accounts are safe. Run as root; the second command counts real hashes.

affected.label: openssh below the fixed package
affected.text: Upstream: OpenSSH before 10.6p2, which works around the bug in sshd; OpenSSH says the root cause is outside sshd. Alpine's fixed packages are listed under Upgrade.

do.label: Upgrade openssh, then restart
do.text: Install the fixed package for your Alpine branch (listed below; fixes go back to 3.16). Run `apk upgrade -U -a`, then `rc-service sshd restart`: upgrading alone leaves the old sshd running. Other musl builds: OpenSSH 10.6p2. musl itself hasn't changed yet: on 9 Nov 2026 its maintainer said musl 1.2.7 will probably stop returning `*` when crypt() fails, but it isn't decided.

do.label: Can't upgrade? Turn off passwords
do.text: In `sshd_config` (or a drop-in in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/` on Alpine 3.19+). Also set any `PasswordAuthentication yes` inside `Match` blocks to no; a drop-in doesn't override those. Check key login works, validate with `sshd -t`, then restart sshd and confirm `sshd -T` shows `passwordauthentication no`.

do.label: Look for break-ins
do.text: A password login for `root`, `alpine` or any key-only user is a red flag. Also review `doas` use, new users, new `authorized_keys` entries and changed files. If you can't rule out a login, treat the host as compromised. US federal agencies must also do forensic triage under the KEV listing.

changes.text: Clarified: the attack also needs another account with a real password hash, and OpenSSH calls 10.6p2 a workaround. Alpine and the CVE record give different working password lengths (257 vs 256 to 1024). musl itself hasn't changed crypt() yet.
Dropped a conflicting Alpine 3.19 tracker version (the package index matches the advisory). Safe versions added.
Review: directory-service accounts, Match blocks, and the CVE record's version and length range added.
Added to CISA KEV, due 12 Nov.
Attacks seen within hours of the fix.
